t: That the first sentence of section 6 of the International Travel Act of 1961, as amended (22 U.S.C. 2126) is amended by striking out “and” immediately after “1978;”, and inserting immediately before the period at the end thereof the following: “; and (8) $8,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1980”.

fable.w: This section only amends the International Travel Act of 1961 to add an authorization of appropriations for fiscal year 1980. There is no tempting reading here: no party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue, and no rulemaking, hearing, or advisory body is involved.
fable.s: $8,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1980

opus.w: This section only amends the International Travel Act of 1961 to add an $8,000,000 authorization for fiscal year 1980. It does not involve any party outside the federal government in a federal decision. It sets out no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue. Being about federal spending does not make it participation.
opus.b:
**Step 1: Analysis.** One might be tempted to read this as being about a decision on federal tourism-promotion spending under the International Travel Act. That reading fails because the section only changes the wording of an existing provision to add an $8,000,000 authorization for fiscal year 1980. No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.

**Step 2: Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section is a legislative amendment that changes a specific dollar amount in a previous statute. It does not establish any process for consulting with, coordinating with, or receiving input from parties outside the federal government. The action described is purely internal to the legislative process of amending statutory text.
qwen_chat.s: That the first sentence of section 6 of the International Travel Act of 1961, as amended (22 U.S.C. 2126) is amended by striking out “and” immediately after “1978;”, and inserting immediately before the period at the end thereof the following: “; and (8) $8,000,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 1980”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that amending a statute involves some form of public input or consultation, but the text itself is purely a legislative amendment to an appropriation figure. It does not describe any process of consulting with outsiders.
